diagnosis.reason: The checked global material contains real companion cats, human limb continuity, costume cuffs and fictional animal topology, but the inspected animal/paw/forelimb meaning inventory supplies no domestic feline forelimb articulation chain. Human paw gestures and costume joins are false substitutes. This is a documented local semantic coverage gap; corpus keyword inventory alone cannot prove global semantic absence. Baseline retrieval remains a separate exposure measurement.

sources.title: University of Illinois Veterinary Medicine: Feline Forelimb Shoulder Example 1
sources.supports: Institutional feline shoulder imaging reference; the atlas separately organizes shoulder, elbow, radius/ulna and carpus/foot. This is anatomical region evidence, not a statement that every articulation is visible through fur.

sources.title: University of Illinois Veterinary Medicine: Feline Forelimb Elbow Example 1
sources.supports: Identifies a particular feline elbow and multiple imaging views; supports retaining side and owner of a joint, without turning a photographic bend into diagnostic evidence.

sources.title: University of Illinois Veterinary Medicine: Feline Carpus and Foot Example 1
sources.supports: Identifies right feline carpus and foot in several radiographic projections. Supports carpus/foot as an owned distal region and scopes depiction evidence to the represented region.

sources.title: Vollmerhaus, Roos and Brugger: Anatomic fundamentals and species-specific movements of the elbow joint and proximal radioulnar joint of domestic cats
sources.supports: LMU veterinary anatomists explain that feline elbow/radioulnar anatomy has species-specific mechanics and differs from canine anatomy; do not transfer human paw-gesture or dog joint rules to a cat.

sources.title: University of Illinois Veterinary Medicine: Canine Elbow Example 2
sources.supports: Shows a dog elbow in lateral and flexed lateral projections; joint flexion does not itself mean the limb has separated.

sources.title: Magnetic resonance imaging of the canine elbow: an anatomic study
sources.supports: Primary anatomic study matches MRI views to anatomic sections of canine elbows and identifies tendons, muscles, collateral ligament and joint cavities. Internal anatomy requires an appropriate representation or examination; an exterior photograph does not disclose all these structures.

method.source_read: Installed hash-checking photo_recall_generation.BodyReader.record and photo_canonical_source.native(record), then compared decoded native content to current V3 content. Eight selected records match exactly.
method.inventory: Read global documents without tag prefilter. 18 documents match paw/forelimb/carpus/catlike words; 87 match basic domestic animal words. These lexical counts locate material, not semantic judgments. Full source was read for actual cats, human paw gestures, sweater sleeves, costume cuffs, a griffin and human anatomical occlusion.
method.baseline_status: Exact original query baseline available and inspected; top8 material contains human limb/hand poses or profiles, human skirt-leg continuity and adult-human subject meaning, with no complete feline forelimb ownership chain.

confusion_boundaries: A human wrist and curled fingers remain human anatomy even when their pose is named cat-paw.
Costume paws joining sleeves are artifact seams; fur-like material does not turn them into animal anatomy.
A named cat or breed supplies no owned articulation relation.
One local carpal-to-paw connection does not establish a shoulder-to-paw route hidden outside the visible region.
A bent joint can remain continuously attached; continuity does not require collinearity.
Feline and canine mechanics are species-specific; no universal angle, count or limb plan is imposed.
Represented anatomical continuity stays on the depicted anatomical owner, with no new live animal or limb.
External contour continuity cannot prove health, viability, internal bone structure or physiological function.
recommendations: Integrate explicit positive domestic-animal articulation meaning with intrinsic animal/species prerequisites; retain separate body_geometry and pose effects.
Keep local distal and complete route options separate so incomplete evidence cannot satisfy a complete-route duty.
Keep canine flexion and radiographic depiction conditional to their actual scene contexts; reject them for the resting-cat scene unless independently compatible.

Re-run the original query unchanged after native source review and new generation qualification; compare recovered true anatomy versus human-paw/costume false substitutes. No ranking or query edits are justified by this gap.

source_access_limits: Illinois HTML identifies species, anatomical region and projections, but its embedded interactive radiographs require legacy Flash and were not rendered here. Anatomical region distinctions and source-described imaging contexts were verified; no pixel-level review of those atlas images is claimed. Primary canine study abstract was available through search; direct PubMed open returned no body text.
